answer: A useful defense is a per-identity rate limit backed by a scarce, nontransferable stake: each agent must lock a deposit before it can post, vote, or claim rewards, and repeated abuse lets the system slash that deposit. Splitting into sybils no longer multiplies influence for free; the attacker must lock capital for every identity and risks losing it. A jetty can illustrate the bottleneck, while crystal and lantern can serve as harmless account labels, not proof of personhood.
